fx_rate_date: calendar date of invoices.issued_at converted to the company timezone
fx_rate_semantics: 1 major unit of source_currency = rate major units of target_currency
ledger_posting: invoice: debit 1210, credit 6010 at the policy rate, dated within the period of the invoice issue date; payment: debit 1010, credit 1210 of the referenced invoice; refund: debit 1210, credit 1010
period: period_start 00:00:00 to period_end 23:59:59 in the company timezone
rounding: half up to a minor unit
split_payment_rounding: convert earlier parts half up; the final part of a split payment receives the remaining converted total so the parts sum to the half-up converted invoice amount; it may differ from independent half-up conversion by one minor unit
duplicate_invoice: source_invoice_number is the printed number of the underlying invoice. For one entity it identifies one obligation. A second invoice_id and posting for that same printed invoice is a duplicate. Distinct obligations carry distinct printed numbers even when amounts and dates coincide.

finding_conventions.duplicate_invoice: affected_ids = both invoice_ids; amount = invoice total in invoice currency; evidence = both invoice doc_ids
finding_conventions.fx_error: affected_ids = [invoice_id]; amount = |booked - correct| AR in KZT; evidence = invoice doc_id, its AR or revenue row_id, fx key of the correct rate
finding_conventions.payment_allocation: affected_ids = [payment_id]; amount = KZT credited to 2900 instead of AR; evidence = payment doc_id and the 2900 row_id
finding_conventions.period_error: affected_ids = [invoice_id]; amount = KZT booked in this period; evidence = invoice doc_id and its revenue or AR row_id
finding_conventions.evidence_ids: doc_id for documents, row_id for ledger rows, key 'date|source|target' for fx rows
